claim.claim-text: 1. An apparatus configured to be employed in a base station (BS), comprising:
a memory interface; and processing circuitry coupled to the memory interface, and when executing instructions stored in the memory interface, configured to cause the BS to:

transmit, to a user equipment (UE), a RRC (Radio Resource Control) configuration information including a RB-bundle-size parameter, the RB-bundle-size parameter defining a resource block (RB) bundle size of a set of RB bundles; and transmit a control signal including wake up signal (WUS) for a DRX-on (Discontinuous Reception On) occasion of a Connected mode DRX, the WUS indicating whether to start the DRX_on occasion, wherein the WUS is transmitted via a first RB bundle of the set of RB bundles applying a first precoder.
2. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the set of RB bundles is respectively constructed by RBs consecutively numbered in an order of time first, then in a frequency domain.

3. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the WUS is transmitted using a set of RBs including both the first RB bundle applying the first precoder and a second RB bundle of the set of RB bundles applying a second precoder.

4. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the processing circuitry is further configured to, upon transmitting the WUS, cause the UE to determine whether to enter a NAM (network access mode) and monitor a PDCCH (Physical Downlink Control Channel).
5. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the first precoder is applied to all RBs within the first RB bundle.
6. The apparatus of claim 5, wherein precoder cycling is performed across different RB bundles for transmitting the WUS.

7. The apparatus of claim 1, wherein a RB bundle of the set of RB bundles comprises y consecutive RBs numbered first in a time domain and then in a frequency domain, wherein y is the RB bundle size configured by the RB-bundle-size parameter.
8. An apparatus configured to be employed in a base station (BS), comprising:
a memory interface; and processing circuitry configured to:

generate, for a UE (User Equipment) in a power saving mode, a power saving signal for a DRX-on (Discontinuous Reception On) occasion of a Connected mode DRX, wherein the power saving signal is a WUS (Wake Up Signal) or a GTS (Go To Sleep signal); and map the power saving signal to a set of RBs (Resource Blocks) with precoder cycling performed across RB bundles.

9. The apparatus of claim 8, wherein the processing circuitry is further configured to generate RRC (Radio Resource Control) configuration information that configures a RB bundle size of the RB bundles.

10. The apparatus of claim 9, wherein the set of RBs includes a first RB bundle of the RB bundle size precoded by a first precoder and a second RB bundle of the RB bundle size precoded by a second precoder.

11. The apparatus of claim 9, wherein a RB bundle of the RB bundles comprises y consecutive RBs numbered first in a time domain and then in a frequency domain, wherein y is the configured RB bundle size.
12. A non-transitory machine readable medium comprising instructions that, when executed, cause a User Equipment (UE) to:

receive a power saving signal associated with a DRX-on (Discontinuous Reception On) occasion of a Connected mode DRX, wherein the power saving signal is received via a set of RBs (Resource Blocks) with precoder cycling performed across RB bundles; and determine, based on the received power saving signal, whether to enter a NAM (network access mode) and monitor a PDCCH (Physical Downlink Control Channel).

13. The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 12, wherein the instructions, when executed, further cause the UE to receive RRC (Radio Resource Control) configuration information that configures a RB bundle size of the RB bundles.

14. The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 13, wherein a RB bundle of the RB bundles comprises y consecutive RBs numbered first in a time domain and then in a frequency domain, wherein y is the configured RB bundle size.

15. The non-transitory machine readable medium of claim 13, wherein the set of RBs includes a first RB bundle of the RB bundle size precoded by a first precoder and a second RB bundle of the RB bundle size precoded by a second precoder.
